column20: What went wrong and why? -- "a change made to the Microsoft Wide Area Network (WAN)"; "a command given to the router caused it to send messages to all other routers"
column21: What went wrong and why? -- "During this re-computation process, the routers were unable to correctly forward packets traversing them"
column22: What happened? -- "customers experienced issues with networking connectivity" to resources in Azure regions and other Microsoft services; "While most regions and services had recovered by 09:00 UTC"
column23: What happened? -- "most regions and services had recovered by 09:00 UTC"; also impacted "Azure Government cloud services"
column24: What went wrong and why? -- "a command given to the router caused it to send messages to all other routers in the WAN, which resulted in all of them recomputing their adjacency and forwarding tables"
column25: How did we respond? -- "By 08:10 UTC, the network started to recover automatically", then residual packet loss until "those systems were manually restarted" (recovery completed 12:43 UTC)
column26: What went wrong and why? / How did we respond? -- "a command given to the router caused it to send messages to all other routers in the WAN"; "our automated systems for maintaining the health of the WAN were paused, including the systems for identifying and removing unhealthy devices, and the traffic engineering system"
